Sons of goats and rams, that's what they are. Pfft. Eh, speaking of which, I doubt you carry much coin with you, so I'll skip the funding part. I heard some humans talking a great deal about Balor having its own moonshine back in the day. Some lad named Vander used to own a farmstead, and he was said to brew a mean drink. I doubt the man lives, but perhaps you'll find some of his brew by his old home?
41813.progress: Hope it's worth the trouble, eh?
41813.completion: Magni's beard, an entire crate of it! So lucky this stuff doesn't go bad easily. Here you go, have some yourself.

41814.title: The Late Duke Balor
41814.description:
I promised the Explorers' League a prize whenever I left Ironforge, mostly because they wounded my pride! I dug here and there, but there wasn't much to find on this side of the island, and I'm not strong enough to take on an entire army of orcs just to fulfill my ambition. As much as it pains me, I might have to return empty-handed.

Unless... How about we make a trade? An heirloom for an heirloom. You scratch my back, I'll scratch yours, that sort of thing. I have this artifact I dug up on another expedition that I'm willing to trade, if you return with something from the Duke's castle. I'm man enough to admit my knowledge of Balor is quite limited, but the late Duke must have had something valuable. A sword, a shield, a crown—whatever you may find, bring it back to me, and we'll make the trade.
41814.progress: Did you come up with something?
41814.completion: While in poor condition, it is still the crown of a duke. This will prove those rascals in the Halls of Explorers wrong! Thank you, <race>. Here is what I promised.

41815.title: Free Merchandise
41815.description:
There's a pirate compound to the northwest—bilgerats, in the purest sense. My guess is they've come here to loot the castle. Too bad it's haunted by ghosts and stalked by demons and their masters, huh?

Anyway, this simply means a job opportunity for both of us. I am a craftsman, a merchant—but above all else, I am a Goblin of Kezan! I could never pass up free merchandise.

Well, "free"... You know—you'll have to loot it from their cold hands. But it's still free, right? Get a move on, then.
41815.completion: Good coin comin' from these. Got your cut right here.

41816.title: The First of Many
41816.description:
Thunder. Roaring thunder. The clouds tremble each time the sky cracks, and so does my body. How I wish I were atop a mighty beast above the clouds, roaring for all to hear! Living up to the name of my clan—Thunderlord—a name soon forgotten by this world. Few share my melancholic heart; it is why I follow him, that grumpy old orc.

Mourning the past serves nothing. The Horde is who we are now. I wish only to pass on the spirit of the hunt, the heart and mind of those who came before, so that they—and I—may live forever.

And you, you are the candle I lit with my fire. One day, from your flame, another will be born.

Find your way to the main island, through the ruined port of Breezhaven. Past the mine and orchard, turn right to find Sorrowmere Lake. Paint yourself with crocolisk blood and return with five of their tails. It has been long since I tasted their meat.

Be bold, be careful—and by all means, be thrilled by the hunt.
41816.progress: Go out there and prove to yourself that you are the predator, not the prey.
41816.completion: I smell blood in the air. You wear it like a second skin now. Good. Bring those tails here—we will feast on them.

41817.title: Fear is Your Rival
41817.description:
A warm feeling, is it not? A successful attempt, one whose bounty you shared with another, bound to you by mutual respect for the hunt.

This moment we share now, I have shared countless times with my people back home. No day would pass without us returning with prey, feasting on our spoils, and telling stories of our hunts.

It is a good life we had—we have. Though even then, many were lost; a simple negligence can cost you your life.

Fear is your rival, my friend. You must control it, or it will gain reign over you. Do not concern yourself with competing against others—compete against your fear. One second is enough for you to perish.

With that in mind, you must return to Sorrowmere Lake and follow the long bridges to the Scurrying Thicket. Your next hunt awaits. Slay the Mistbark Spiders, and see how you fare against an enemy of many legs and a poisonous bite.

As you walk there, remember what I told you: it is not truly them you are fighting, but your fear.
41817.progress: Life is a battle, a battle against the aspects of your being that you cannot fully control.
41817.completion: Your fear did not win today. Your eyes have changed, they look calmer now.

41818.title: We are not Born Equal
41818.description:
A far more challenging hunt, but many more await. A lesson you must learn is that no creature is born equal. Those who say otherwise lack vision or common sense.

On your journeys, you will face many trials. Azeroth is vast and cruel; you must be ready for anything.

Inequality also marks our uniqueness. Do not see the word "unequal" and sink into dark thoughts. Look beyond, understand that while the world may not bow to you, being yourself is enough. You will find a way, your way, and you will be unique.

You have faced your fear, and that was the first step to finding your own path.

Now, return to the main island. Where the road splits at the orchard, take a left and pass through the ruined castle walls. Beyond the church and crypt, find the other entrance. Go past it, and past the cave. In the loose hills beyond, you will find buzzards and vultures. Face them, and learn to battle a flying enemy.
41818.completion: I am proud of the hunter you have become. Choose something of mine to carry as a memento of your success.

41819.title: A Dark Tide Will Rise
41819.description:
I have never taken a liking to the taste of fish—mostly because it was such a frequent meal on the Darkspear Isles. Yet, ever since we were forced to leave our home, it is not the taste but the memories it brings that trouble me. The foul Sea Witch, her naga, and their mindless murloc minions cost our people dearly. Though I cling not to the past, I cannot help but feel a burning desire to see these filthy creatures slain.

I foresee a great future for our tribe within the Horde, much like my father and grandfather before me. I proudly bear its flag, yet my thoughts betray me on this day. So, I task you, one who will help shape the future of the Horde alongside me, to slay the Muckgills on your path to eliminate the shadowy leader who hides among them.

Climb down the hill and in that cave you will find them guarding the entrance for whatever plot the Sea Herald may have.
41819.progress: Slithering snakes, self acclaimed rulers of the seas and oceans—-a pain to deal with.
41819.completion: The irony of this scroll is lost on me.

41820.title: To My Father, Vol'jin
41820.description:
My duty is to remain here and see the Shadow Council brought to an end. Yet, I cannot help but reflect on what this truly means. For the Sea Witch to resurface after such a long time, it is haunting. You must understand, my people have lost a great deal because of her. Though I may be repeating myself, it is because I seek your empathy.

I am unable to leave this place. Though my feet ache to move, I cannot bear the thought of leaving Kilrogg and our allies to face this alone. I am but a single troll, true, but I have grown fond of the old chieftain, to be fair. He is gruesome, yet wise. Passionate and explosive, there is much I can learn from him. One day, I will take the mantle of Darkspear chieftain, and with it comes great responsibility.

This orc has endured many hardships, and his shoulders are heavy still. I will give him the chance to nurture the next generation of the Horde through me. And so, I ask you to deliver this scroll to my father, in Grommash Hold.
41820.progress: There is little time to spare. Speak.
41820.completion: O'jin is on the right path; he has done well to send you instead of coming himself. A chieftain must know how to make the proper choice. This is valuable information, and for your trouble, a reward is due. There may come a time when I will seek your aid in dealing with this issue. I will return to my duties and soon speak with the Warchief. Beware of the shadows, <name>, especially where they dance freely.

41821.title: Innocence Lost
41821.description:
Whispers come and go; the spirits are ever restless here. But even with all this chatter, there are a few voices I cannot silence.

The enemy is foul, vile, and beyond any salvation for what they have done. I hear it—so loud and clear—I can hear it.

An abomination, born of cruel intent, of a soulless wretch. I cannot stand it anymore.

You must find your way into that castle and put it down. I cannot describe it in words—you must see it for yourself. It's haunting.

You must slay it, slay it to set them free—those poor, young souls.

Leave no Stormreaver alive; they must suffer the wrath of the living world so the ones beyond may rest.

Go now. Just go. You will know it when you see it...
41821.completion: I will light a torch and perform a ritual to guide their souls to the afterlife. Thank you for setting them free.

41822.title: Grim Sunlight
41822.description:
Made by the hands of men, the only light still visible across Balor is kept prisoner just under our noses. A lighthouse—a strange form of artificial light. The world is vast beyond the villages of my tribe, and the Earthmother holds many children—but some, she was forced to adopt.

The Horde is no stranger to them either, and as much as I would like to say otherwise, I do not think I will ever look upon them with true empathy. A specter of respect? Pity, perhaps. Nevertheless, I am straying from the purpose of our conversation.

Under the gaze of that lighthouse, you will find many so-called Mystics, though you may seek them elsewhere if you wish.

I task you with slaying as many as you can. The empty shells of fel corruption, and their rotting flesh will serve as nourishment in time, allowing nature to take its course once more.
41822.progress: In time, An'she will return to these lands.
41822.completion: A mercy far too great for scum like them. Take these; they will carry the light of An'she with you through grim lands.

41823.title: Living Fungus
41823.description:
Among the ruined battlefield, a cave can be found—an old mine, perhaps. It is there that I have sensed an unnatural disturbance.

Something once immobile has risen on its own feet to live. Much like the undead scattered across this ruined land, these creatures are mindless and will attack any on sight.

I task you to go there, find them, and slay some. I will need samples, so be sure to bring something sharp. With those samples, I can study what made them rise.

I should tell you beforehand—this will not aid our efforts to remove the Stormreaver—but I will have a reward ready for you.

Do not make me wait.
41823.progress: This task can wait, but I would rather you fulfill it as quickly as possible.
41823.completion: You have my thanks—and with them, a reward.

41824.title: Mycellakos
41824.description:
These samples have a dark feeling to them. I don't know if you can tell, but it seems they have been infused with some sort of magic—magic that brought them into a state of life.

From what I can tell, they resemble the boggling creatures of Kalimdor, yet are far more twisted. I have yet to attempt cleansing them, though truth be told, this is just dead tissue at this point.

I believe these living fungi originate from a common source. To speak plainly, there should be a larger one that infected the rest. I say this not simply on a whim, but because I feel something from the isle—around the area of the ruined castle—rather, under it.

I believe the source of contamination comes from there. If you can find your way beneath the castle, you might uncover the answers we seek.

Return anything you deem important to me.
41824.progress: The Earthmother will guide you to the answer.
41824.completion: You have brought me its core? Well done. I will attempt to purify it now.

41825.title: The Matron Will Know
41825.description:
Purifying this core is well beyond my abilities. As much as I hate to admit it, there is no way I can do this alone.

It is with a heavy heart that I part with this core; I wished for nothing more than to research it and uncover what caused it to become alive. Nevertheless, this is knowledge that must be passed on.

There is someone who will surely know how to handle the core—our Matron. You will find her in Thunder Bluff, at the Elder Rise.

Pay no mind to Cor and Grom; I will give you my mark, and you will be able to walk freely past them.

Do not speak too much before the Matron. She has a short fuse, and—believe it or not—I have grown fond of you.
41825.completion:
Uda'pe was right to send you to me. Though we are not very fond of working with the Horde, you have my thanks and will be paid accordingly.

I will even add a bonus for being so silent and respectful—Uda'pe taught you well.

41826.title: Those That Remain
41826.description:
A fistful of ash. That is what I always believed my fate to be. Yet fate had other plans. Instead of falling to the fire I once commanded, I succumbed to the cold embrace of the Twisting Nether. A fitting end for one who abandoned his ancestors and embraced the Burning Legion.

Still, I curse my fate. I followed my chieftain—my elder, Ner'zhul. Where the elements once spoke, I listened. But I betrayed them. Demonic whispers filled the void, and I welcomed them. I was stronger than ever. I do not fully regret my path; I still wield the power granted by our former masters.

What I seek now is vengeance, upon all who claim to follow Gul'dan. My soul, trapped in a shard, was denied death. And now I stand in the rotting flesh of a woman foolish enough to challenge the Horde. There is no rest for the wicked, but not all retain their sense of self. Travel to the Ruins of Breezehaven, and lay to rest those that remain.
41826.progress: None are deserving of such a cruel fate.
41826.completion: Mindless undead. Some are nothing more than flesh waiting to be cut down; others, the lingering essences of those who were—forever trapped. You have fulfilled your task.

41827.title: Old Friend
41827.description:
I was never one for irony. Yet I cannot help but see it in this scenario. In the end, only fools seem to be smiled upon by luck—so I suppose. When Gul'dan never returned from the Tomb of Sargeras, everyone agreed that he, and those who followed him on that fool's errand, had lost their lives.

Yet one survived, and he is here. Stranded on a turtle's back, returned from the Broken Isles. I don't yet know if he's here to aid the scum hiding on this isle, or if his purpose mirrors ours. What I do know is this: having him on our side—or at the very least, getting some information out of him—will be worth our time.

Beyond the small island of the lighthouse, swim ahead and you'll find his hut. Just get out of this cave and go straight. But beware the murlocs haunting the waters. And when you see him... spit in his face for me. Or don't. Your call.
41827.completion: Mok'gun's fate was sealed by Gul'dan. He was not the first nor the last. Rest easy, stranger. This old wanderer has no quarrel with you or your kin. I am Drak'thul, once a powerful warlock of the Stormreaver Clan. Now I am here to make sure I am the last of my kind.

41828.title: Bugs on My Island
41828.description:
Years ago, when our people first set foot in this world, we believed ourselves invincible. Before the First War truly began, joined by that filthy two-headed mongrel Cho'gall, we brought ruin to the human lands. Our armies marched to the gates of Stormwind City, and victory was within reach. We were clearly the superior warriors.

Arrogance, young one. The greatest enemy of those who deem themselves strong. From the gates, mounted warriors struck like lightning. Backed by magic, these knights forced this proud chieftain to retreat with his tail between his legs. Humility—a trait every warrior ready to die in battle must carry. Always assume your enemy is stronger. Always believe that, if you survive, you will be stronger than before.

Do not underestimate humanity. Leave this camp without caution, and you may find a dagger in your back. They skulk in the shadows, closer than is comfortable. They may not be our main focus but find and slay them.
41828.completion: Stand proud child of the Horde. Victory is honorably achieved by those with strength and thunder in their blood.

41829.title: Eyes of Stormreaver
41829.description:
In their eternal mockery, these foolish warlocks have named one of their abilities after my missing eye. There is no way I can accept this insult with a straight face. It is a disgrace—to my name, to all that I am!

Were I not stuck here under this wretched tent by whatever mischievous power compels me to trust you instead of exacting my own justice, I would march out myself and collect the eyes of those blasted, fel-hungry oafs.

But as I am denied that right, you will do it in my stead. Venture back to the island of Balor and slay the Stormreaver Warlocks. Bring me no fewer than thirty of their eyes! They say if you believe in “an eye for an eye,” the world will one day go blind. The Stormreavers won't need their sight any longer—not once you're done with them.
41829.progress: I am prepared to set them aflame.
41829.completion: Good. Now I shall burn these wretched eyes, so the last thing their souls gaze upon is the fiery pits of the afterlife they deserve.

41830.title: Deep in the Mines
41830.description:
I bid you welcome to the legacy of crime of that which you call home—shelter, family. Witness the havoc brought by the hands of the slaving Horde. This is what would have remained of all Azeroth, were we not rid of our demonic masters. Take it in. And then focus—we are not here to conquer, nor to save. We are here to assume responsibility.

As always, the cursed mongrels of the Shadow Council do not fail to make their sort as detestable as one could be. Were it not enough that their numbers plague this war-scarred land, they have gone above and beyond to raise both flesh and soul beyond the veil of death.

In what was Breezehaven, you will find a mine. Dispatch the numbers of bones and rotting flesh that stand between you and their pitiful masters. Find these so-called necromancers and stain your blade with their fel-ridden blood. I owe a personal debt to the scum that dared call themselves Stormreaver. What even is a storm in the face of a hollow that will swallow all there is?
41830.progress: We owe apologies to none. It is not guilt that brought us here—but honor.
41830.completion: I see the color of blood and smell the stench of death on you. Well done. Now, onto other matters.

41831.title: Mere Thoughts
41831.description:
Since I have regained my freedom, I have come to think about many things. Many questions have riddled my mind into labyrinths I have struggled to overcome. It was for that reason alone I chose to step aside for some time. However, I did not expect to be so easily forgotten. Mere thoughts.

In my short-lived hermit life, I was once or twice challenged to duel the notion of evilness. Are we born evil—or do we become so later on, due to circumstances? The conclusion I came to was quite simple: we all bear a seed of evil at the root of our own being, but it is by choice whether it grows or not.

Which brings us to your next task. If you believe my words earlier to be nothing but a bore, hear me now. Havoc is what they know, so havoc is what you will give. Go beyond Breezehaven, push closer to the castle—your targets await. You are not a killer—you are the consequence of their actions, coming to take its due.
41831.progress: How thin the line between arrogance and confidence can be.
41831.completion: Today, you have been the consequence of others. One day, your own will find you.

41832.title: Colony of Ants
41832.description:
Are you one to care for insects, soldier? I have taken a keen interest in ants. You see, while they differ in species, hierarchy, and even customs, were you to open your mind to see them so—there is only one truth. The moment the queen dies, three things can happen: the colony falls apart, slowly dying without new workers; it has more than one queen, so they still survive; or it raises a new queen to ensure the colony endures.

Just like ants, the Stormreaver Clan numbers many. Your efforts, while not in vain, have barely dealt any damage to their true strength. So, to ensure the goal of our mission, you must go once again and clear us a path—this time, closer to their nest. Travel to the Ruins of Stromwrought Castle. Do not hold back. Go as far as you can. In that everlasting battlefield, you will be the boot that stomps over the colony.

Adventure not alone—seek aid from your brothers and sisters.
41832.progress: The queens of the colony are close. Keep a level head and push forward.
41832.completion: You know victory like no other—I'm half a mind to challenge you myself.

41833.title: It Can't Rain All the Time
41833.description:
If you have yet to seek Drak'thul, now is the time. Drak'thul holds the key to storm the castle, and your next task is to put it all to rest. An old acquaintance has paid me a visit. Though we do not see eye to eye on many things, there is one hatred we share—the hatred for a despicable being who stood beside Gul'dan during the forming of this clan.

Though the coward is not here himself, he has sent his most treasured pupil to oversee the new uprising. While he is your main target, do not shy away from slaying all you lay eyes upon—Dagar and Oronok especially. Steel yourself; I have no clue what they have in store for you.

While my hatred for them burns like the lowest pits of Blackrock Mountain, I know better—I know they are capable, though despicable. But I believe you are even more capable. Reach out to your allies once more, and see it done. I do wonder... will the sun return to this island once I see you return? After all, it can't rain all the time.
41833.progress: Ashes to ashes, dust to dust and scum to scum.
41833.completion: Well, what do you know... a ray of sunshine breaks through.

41834.title: Storm's End
41834.description:
When I was sent to this island, I believed the Warchief—like most—saw only an old orc, ready to die. He ordered me to serve as a commander, not a warrior. Were it not for Eitrigg's counsel and Saurfang's mocking words, I doubt I would have played my part. But I trusted my friends, and they trusted the Warchief.

A Frostwolf heart beats in his chest. He is wise beyond his years, much like Drek'thar and Orgrim. It seems he was right about me. Though I longed to fight at your side, to stain this island red with my axe, I have learned something else.

I am the last chieftain of the Bleeding Hollow, elder of the Horde, and with these hands, I will guide the next generation. Go now, with victory in your heart, to Grommash Hold. Present our triumph to the Warchief, and tell him I will soon return. Perhaps I will visit Hellscream's memorial when I do.
41834.completion:
Though it is not bound to be the last time we see the embers of the Shadow Council, a great victory was won. While we wish nothing from the land of Balor, it has given me the greatest gift.

Kilrogg was spiteful in the beginning, jealous of Grommash's celebration as a hero—while he himself seemed forgotten. But he was wrong to envy Grommash. My older brother merely set the foundation. It is you, and I, and Kilrogg who will build our future. I am glad he sees it that way now.

41835.title: Legion or Not, Here I Come
41835.description:
While they already occupy most of the island, it seems they have not truly bathed in their own arrogance. As if expecting both Alliance and Horde to come, a great number of demons have been summoned. I can feel their echoing presence from this far. Whether it is for protection or invasion, I know not.

Nor does it truly matter, since you will thwart their plans. You can find these demons in a cave near the south west end of the island. Just past the ruined battlefields west of Stormwrought castle. While the imps may not prove a real challenge, you will have to deal with felhunters and succubi.

I do wonder—will you succumb to the fire of an imp, the gluttony of the felhunter, or perhaps the lust of the succubi? I truly hope not, for your role here has yet to end. I will offer you a healthstone—not that I don’t trust you, but it is best to have the means to heal when the unexpected strikes, is it not?
41835.progress: Legion or not, do what must be done.
41835.completion: A step closer to the true goal.

41836.title: Lady Who?
41836.description:
I am sure you are eager to take the battle to the castle at any cost as soon as possible. But for you to do so we must first find the key to open it. Inside the same cave I have sent you to hunt the demons summoned by the Stormreaver Clan you will also find one that has claimed leadership over the rest. She calls herself Lady Harelyss.

This demon holds a great importance, simply because–if my own minions speak the truth, she holds an item that will secure us the key to the castle. While I cannot have you return her here, since you would have to drag her through a battlefield, I will give you a soulshard–the minute you deal the final blow, you will capture her soul in it, simply by having it on you.

Make sure to retrieve the item we are indeed looking for, her demise is inevitable and capturing her soul is simply our insurance in case we need to gather more information.
41836.progress: I wonder what sort of dark, twisted artefact she holds that can provide her ownership of a copy of the key.
41836.completion:
<Drak'thul cracks the box open.>

What is this...?

41837.title: Storm, Twilight and Hammer
41837.description:
The Stormreaver Clan was not composed solely of orcs from the Shadow Council, but also included the ogre magi who served under Cho'Gall. While a questionable ally, Gul'dan kept that two-headed buffoon as close as he could. I do wonder if the reason was that he knew they would one day betray each other in their lust for power.

Alas, one failed while the other lives—hiding beneath the sands, behind the cloak of a cult that worships myths and legends as old as this world. I have taken the liberty of making the succubi share their plans with me. To the west, past the cave where you defeated her, you will find the Windrock Cliffs. It is there that a member of the Twilight's Hammer holds a fragment of the key. Slay him and return with whatever you find.
41837.progress: The lockbox merely contained the first fragment.
41837.completion: Both fragments together will now serve as the key to enter the ruins of the castle. Beware, for you will face both servants of the Legion and cultists of those long forgotten.

41838.title: Trouble at Slickwick Oil Rig
41838.description:
Hey, you! You seem like a tough fella, and a tough fella is just what we need. Down south near the mountains of Thistleshrub Valley, we started with our newest big money making plan, the Slickwick Oil Rig. Everything went smooth for a while, until the pump stations went crazy and the oil started to move on its own! I’ve trotted throughout the entire desert back to Gadgetzan to get some help for our problem, and you look like just the <class> we need! Don’t worry, we’ll pay you a fat sum of glorious gold! Once you reach the southern mountains, near the big cacti you’ll find a slope up the mountain range. The oil rig is not far from there. Talk to Assistant Steamflare, she’ll know I sent you.

Oh, and could you clean up some of the oil on your way there? Will be worth the effort, trust me!
41838.progress: And who are you? We don’t need bootlickers coming in to waste the boss’ time!
41838.completion: So Blaxbi managed to fulfill his job after all. Excellent. Seeing how you’re still in good shape, you may be useful to us - we’ll see. Take a look around town and see where you can help out. But remember: don’t touch ANYTHING!

41840.title: All That Is Left
41840.description: <Among the puddle left behind by the monstrosity, you find a badly damaged wooden sword. Its size is tiny and the ooze's acid etched most of its surface. You can, however, decipher the words “Sir Tim-” on the toy's hilt. Perhaps that is enough to know who it belonged to.>
41840.progress:
<Judith is still sobbing.>

Oh, Sara, my darling angel… By the Light, please let my Timothy be safe…!
41840.completion:
What…? What is this? Where did you…?! No, no, no! Timothy! My little Timmy, no! Oh, Light, why have you forsaken me?! He was just a boy, my sweet, innocent boy!

<Judith is breaking down. Hysteric crying and yelling is all she can do right now. You did what you could. Atleast she has certainty now.>

41841.title: Artifact of the Dark Lady
41841.description:
<In your hand is the broken Bloodstone Pendant used by Ighal’for, disciple of the deranged Cho’gall, to summon the abhorrent beholder Mergothid into Azeroth. The wounds of the fierce battle against the demon are still strewn across your body. Blood runs down your arm onto your palm. Suddenly, the pendant shakes violently, letting out a twisted shriek while drawing in the red liquid. Shortly after, the blood is gone - and the pendant starts pulsating.

You remember assisting a Forsaken warden in Tarren Mill recovering similar artifacts; relics that belonged to the Dark Lady, Sylvanas Windrunner. It’d be best to return her stolen trinkets back to her.>
41841.progress: Speak quickly. I don’t intend to waste my time with vermin.
41841.completion:
Look what the cat dragged in. I was assuming Wordeen had atleast a smidgeon of competency left in his body, but I was sorely mistaken, it seems. To think one of my artifacts escaped those irritating mages and ended up in the clutches of the Shadow Council. Curious, indeed…

<name>, with the return of the pendant, I am closing the book on this unfortunate circumstance among my subordinates. The traitors have been dealt with, my relics are secured and you… You shall be rewarded for delivering a decisive strike against those misusing my possessions.

41842.title: Antiquities
41842.description:
If you’re entering Stormwrought Castle, I have one humble request for you. The Balor family amassed countless books and tomes over the many years they held authority over the island. Following decades of trade, they collected a sheer unimaginable amount of knowledge in their library. One of them, the personal teachings and lectures on the hidden practices of trade by Sir Walton Balor, younger brother of the second Duke of Balor, is a book both I and Stormwind are very much interested in.

Should you come across the vast library of Stormwrought Castle, search it for said book. And <name>: Beware of the dangers inside. I dare not think about the terrors that await you within those vile halls.
41842.progress: Stormwind always envied the Balorians on perfecting the art of successful trade not only with them, but several other nations as well. It’d be a shame if that knowledge would be lost in time, no?
41842.completion: Oh, more dusty than my grandmother back in Ironforge. Time has not been kind to this old tome, and the humid air is not exactly helping either. I will seal it properly in my chest and begin analysis back in the SI:7 headquarters. For you, <name>, my heartfelt gratitude. Please choose a reward fitting for your service.

41843.title: Assassin In Training
41843.description:
So the time to infiltrate Stormwrought Castle has finally come. This den of devils will demand every last bit of your focus and skill for you to come back in one piece. I won’t mince my words, but you’re surely aware of it yourself already, no? The others and I will secure the perimeter on the castle courtyard to prevent reinforcements halting your operations.

Operative Gillian has ordered you to dispatch the head of the hydra, which is undoubtedly the most crucial task of all. Still, to ensure no resurgence occurs by surviving figureheads, we need to make sure to snuff them out as well. Liquidate any tough guy you come across. We don’t want to deal with that scum again.
41843.progress: I am sure you will run into more than enough fitting candidates for my task there.
41843.completion: Most impressive. It’s a shame you're not cut out for this field of work. Don’t get me wrong, you possess the skills and wits necessary, but I know your adventurous spirit cannot be tamed and seeks the grandeur of Azeroth. Still, the SI:7 owes you much, so let me reward you appropriately for all you’ve done.

41844.title: The Dead Can’t Complain
41844.description:
When we crashlanded here on this island, we noticed that most of our cargo had dropped into the wide expanses of the ocean. While we still have a good chunk of it secured, it’s not nearly enough to satisfy our recipients in Booty Bay. Yunie and the others have their hands full repairing the zeppelin and making sure we don’t actually get eaten by monstrous crustaceans. I on the other hand had the golden opportunity to scout the island when we were looking for Verix a while back. And wouldn’t you know it: there is a giant castle atop the cliffs. You can probably guess what I am hinting at. While I am not as crazy and suicidal as Verix, I would be remiss to pass up this opportunity to grab some valuables no goblin has ever seen before.

Which is where you come in. Grab some friends or pay someone if you don’t have any and grab as many valuables as you can get from within that castle on the other side of Balor. It will pay off, trust me!
41844.progress: You’re tough - or foolish - enough to come to this cursed place on your own, so I’m sure you’ll have no problems going in there and coming back out unharmed - mostly, atleast.
41844.completion: Wow, what a haul. Might not be exactly what we were supposed to be delivering, but I doubt those greedy bastards in their pirate cove will complain that much. Thank you so much, <name>. We owe you big time. You can have this for your troubles, it always gave me the best of luck - the fact I’m still here is proof of that.

41845.title: The Will of Balor
41845.description:
Aberrations skulk these halls. Monsters born from malice and demons from the depth of depravity call this once resplendent place their home. I still remember it vividly, Balor - how it used to be. Bustling with life and commerce. None of it remains, except the spirits of those still clinging on. The cruelty inflicted upon us decades ago tethers us to our former home, preventing us from moving on. Good <class>, will you be the one to break our shackles?

Deep within the castle, beyond the stockades, the orc’s demonic allies conduct vile experiments. One of their overseers, a vile demoness with wings and hooves, holds a fragment of my soul, keeping me frozen in time. Slay her and retrieve it. Then perhaps…
41845.progress: She is a sadistic creature, torturing souls for her own enjoyment. Her retribution cannot come sooner.
41845.completion: Ah… The weight that leaves my very being dissipates as we speak. Being whole once more, passing into the afterlife may not be just a desperate plea anymore. <class>, my sincerest thank you. Had it been not for you, I and many others would have been anchored in the world of the living still. My heart rests more easily now, thanks to you. Please, accept one of my remaining physical possessions as a just reward for you.

41846.title: The Grim Reaches
41846.description:
The Wildhammer kin of Dun Kithas are in dire need of aid. The Dragonmaw Clan grows bolder by the day, and Magistrate Hurdam Toughhand fears they'll strike at any moment!

While we ready our forces for a proper defense, it falls upon us to call upon adventurers such as yourself to lend a hand. Ye've been chosen to assist Magistrate Hurdam and the folk of Dun Kithas in this critical hour.

To reach Grim Reaches, travel through the High Pass—a mountain tunnel near the Farstrider Lodge in Loch Modan. Stay sharp, for the Dragonmaw are no trifling threat. Once you reach Dun Kithas, report to Magistrate Hurdam without delay. May the mountain's strength guide ye!
41846.progress: A newcomer in Dun Kithas! Welcome, welcome.
41846.completion: Ah, welcome to Dun Kithas, <name>! Truly, it lifts me heart to see new faces in our midst. Dark days are looming over us, no doubt, and every pair of hands shall be vital in the trials ahead.

41847.title: Honoring Old Alliances
41847.description:
There was a time, long ago, when we stood united with the noble Wildhammer Dwarves, an alliance forged in mutual respect and necessity. In our time of greatest need, they did not falter. Aerie Peak opened its gates to hundreds of refugees, and their stalwart mountaineers shielded countless caravans from the dangers of the wilds. Their actions, noble and selfless, are a debt we will carry for eternity, though no amount of gratitude could ever repay them.

So it is with a heavy heart that I hear of the plight facing the settlement of Dun Kithas, nestled within the distant and perilous Grim Reaches. In their time of danger, we cannot remain idle. I have already dispatched a detachment of our finest rangers to aid them, but I trust they will accept any additional hands with the warmth of their legendary hospitality.

When you arrive in Dun Kithas, seek out Ranger Swiftstride. She has been entrusted with a most delicate task, one your skills may be called upon to assist. Go with haste, for every moment counts.
41847.completion:
Lord Theron has sent you, has he?

<Ranger Faellina peers intently at you>

If he deems you worthy of this task, then I suppose I need not question his judgment. Very well. Pay close attention, for what I am about to reveal must not be taken lightly. This is no mere errand, and the weight of it should not fall upon ears that do not understand its gravity.

41848.title: To Cure the Withered
41848.description:
You must have seen them — the Withered — when you walked the paths of Alah'thalas. Wretched beings... their thirst for the arcane has consumed their minds, leaving only husks behind.

A tragedy, truly. And what wounds the spirit most is knowing their numbers grow with each passing dawn. The Withering, once begun, cannot be undone — only delayed. But even that demands a torrent of mana, a price many deem too high for those already lost to the hunger...

Yet, Lord Theron holds hope. He believes that these very lands may hold the key to a cure. A slender hope, but hope nonetheless.

Still, all in due course. For now, I have a task for you. Word travels of an ancient, destroyed passage to Grim Batol, somewhere westward, buried among the hills. Should the tales speak true and you uncover this forgotten way... return to me with haste.
41848.progress: Be wary. These lands are teeming with Dragonmaw orcs.
41848.completion: So... the tales whispered by the dwarves of Dun Kithas held truth after all. Curious. One must wonder just how many hidden, long-forgotten passages into Grim Batol yet remain buried beneath stone and time... and what vile things may have once crept forth from their shadows.

41849.title: To Cure the Withered
41849.description:
Now then... There is an old legend that speaks of a dwarven jewelcrafter who once dwelled in this very part of Grim Batol. His craft was unmatched — the gems he forged, said to shimmer with the brilliance of starlight itself.

But more than mere beauty... it is said he could shape crystals capable of storing mana — not only that, but crystals that could be replenished, again and again, without fracturing. A rare and wondrous feat, if ever there was one.

You see where this leads, I trust? Should we recover even a single such gem, our arcanists might unravel the secret of its making. The burden of crafting mana crystals could be lifted... and with that, perhaps, we could better tend to the Withered.

If you would brave the ruins and seek any trace of these enchanted stones — a fragment, a clue, or best of all, a crystal still whole — it would be a boon to our people beyond measure.
41849.progress: Is there truly no hope left for our kin?
41849.completion:
You've found it... By the Sunwell, I can scarcely believe it.

<Ranger Feallina lifts the crystal, tilting it toward the light. The sun dances across its flawless facets, refracting a cascade of colors.>

This... this is no mere gem. It is a masterpiece — a testament to craftsmanship long thought lost.

You have our deepest thanks, <class>. We will move swiftly now — the rangers and I shall descend upon the site and recover as many of these crystals as we can... before reporting back to Lord Theron.

You have rendered a great service to the Quel'dorei this day, my friend. May the light of the stars guide your path always.

41850.title: The Gemstone of Naraz
41850.description:
Just beyond these hills to the east lie the Sal'Galaz Mines. Aye, they've been worked by the stout folk of Dun Kithas for decades – that is, until the troggs came. The miners, curse their greed, likely broke into some old, dark tunnels where those filthy creatures were lurking.

Now, I'd not fret much over it usually – plenty of wealth beneath the ground in these parts – but there's something about those mines. Something rare. Just before the troggs turned up, the miners uncovered a gemstone in the southernmost shaft. And not just any gemstone, mind you. If the tales are true, this could be the Gemstone of Naraz, forged by the very Makers themselves.

I must have it. But I'm no fighter, and those troggs are too much for me. Bring me that gemstone, and you'll have your reward, I swear it.
41850.completion:
The Gemstone of Naraz... Wait a moment—this isn't right! Look at it—this isn't how it's meant to be! It's only half of it, see here? It's cleanly cut, right along this edge! You didn't tamper with it, did you?

...No, no, of course not. That cut's far too precise for anyone without the proper tools—or skill, for that matter. Hmm... this complicates things, but don't start panicking just yet! I've an idea where the other half might be.

41851.title: The Gemstone of Naraz
41851.description:
Prospector Hammertoe was sent off to the Badlands to dig up relics of the Makers. Fool's always had an eye for old treasures, and he was convinced the Gemstone of Naraz might be there. We didn't see eye to eye on it, so we went our separate ways—I took my search to the Grim Reaches instead. Turns out, we were both right in a way. The gemstone's split in two.

But that doesn't matter now. What does matter is I need you to head to the Badlands, to his excavation site, and find the gemstone. If they've uncovered it, well... I doubt Hammertoe will notice if it goes missing.

You bring it to me, understood? The Gemstone of Naraz must be mine—to restore it to its true form.
41851.progress: Hammertoe probably set up camp close to Angor Fortress. That's what I would do, at least. The place is well known for its ancient relics.
41851.completion:
Hammertoe... attacked by the Dark Irons, you say? Bah, we were rivals more often than not and rarely saw eye to eye, but still, this news sits heavy on me. I can only hope he found a way to escape.

But there's no time to dwell on that now! The second half of the Gemstone—just as the old texts described! You've done well, adventurer, truly well. Thank you, thank you! I'll take it to Ironforge at once. With the right hands and the right tools, it'll be restored to its full glory!

41852.title: Earthen Relics
41852.description:
<class>! The Explorers' League is in dire need of your aid!

Word must've reached your ears by now—our dig site, just north of here, has been savagely attacked by those blasted Shadowforge dwarves! The brutes ambushed us, cut down our brethren, and started digging like rabid beasts, with no respect for the archaeological process or the sacred ruins of the Earthen!

I need you to head there, and recover any Earthen relics that might've survived their reckless plundering. Please, time is against us—the very legacy of our kin hangs in the balance!
41852.progress: I beg you, adventurer! Time is of the essence.
41852.completion:
While nothing can bring back our fallen brethren, you've ensured their sacrifice wasn't for nothing. These relics you've recovered are priceless treasures of knowledge, and they'll undoubtedly deepen our understanding of the Earthen and our ancestors' legacy.

On behalf of the Explorers' League, I thank you, <class>. You've done us and our kin a great service.

41853.title: Groldan's Grudge
41853.description:
This will not stand! By my beard, I swear vengeance upon the Shadowforge and their vile lot!

I led the Explorers' League excavation here in the Grim Reaches, a peaceful endeavor, mind you. Then, out of nowhere, those treacherous Dark Irons attacked us under cover of night! Only a handful of us escaped with our lives—most of my comrades were slaughtered where they stood!

We must strike back! Head northeast to my old excavation site and slay as many of those Dark Iron scum as you can. Bring me their heads as proof. Show them no mercy—they deserve none.

And listen—if by any chance you come across my personal stash there, bring it back to me. It holds valuable notes from the excavation, notes I cannot afford to lose!
41853.completion:
<Groldan glares at the heads you've brought him and spits on the ground.>

Ha! That'll send a clear message to those Shadowforge rats! It's only a matter of time before word of this reaches their so-called leadership. Let this be a lesson to them—think twice before crossing the dwarves of Ironforge, or pay the bloody price!

41854.title: Groldan's Stash
41854.description: You find a stash filled with notes, artifacts, and various pieces of junk. The name 'Groldan Blackforge' is written on the lock.
41854.completion:
Ha! Aye, that's me stash, sure as stone!

Thought I'd lost it to those thrice-cursed Dark Irons — but seems the sorry louts hadn't the wit to understand how valuable me notes really are!

<Groldan grumbles as he rummages through the pile, tossing aside old tools and scraps>

Now where'd I put it... Bah, always buryin' the good stuff under junk... Ah! There it is!

Here — take these potions. It's not much, but it ought to serve ye well out there. Consider it a proper thanks from Groldan Blackforge. Just don't go wastin' it on chasin' rabbits or pokin' trolls, aye?

41855.title: Reclaiming Sal'Galaz
41855.description:
My name's Kegg Boulderboots, and I've been foreman of the Sal'Galaz mines for a good thirty years... Everything was going fine—better than fine, really. The mines are rich, bursting with iron and coal.

But then... then we uncovered that cursed gemstone. From the moment we unearthed it, troggs started swarming out of crevices and tunnels like a plague. They overran us in no time.

By the grace of the Makers, most of the miners managed to escape, but the mine itself—it's lost! And with the Dragonmaw threat looming, the city council can't spare a single soldier to help us take it back.

Please, <race>, I'm begging you—help me. Slay 10 Bonesplitter Troggs and 10 Bonesplitter Bonesnappers in the quarry. It's the only chance we have to reclaim what's ours!
41855.progress: I hold no grudge against the Magistrate. I understand that the Dragonmaw threat is more important than the mines.
41855.completion: By the Makers, that's splendid news! With the quarry back in our hands, we're one step closer to reclaiming the mines and restoring what's been lost!

41856.title: Reclaiming Sal'Galaz
41856.description:
I've one more favor to ask of you, <race>.

The quarry may be clear of troggs for now, but the true source of the infestation lies deeper—in the mines themselves. If we're to retake the place for good, you'll need to venture into the mines and deal with the threat at its heart.

Kill at least 10 Bonesplitter Skullthumpers and 10 Bonesplitter Geomancers. Hopefully, that'll be enough to stem the tide... for now.
41856.progress: We dug too deep... too greedily. Now we're paying the price for our folly.
41856.completion:
Amazing work, <race>! I'll send the miners in at once. In just a few days, we'll be back to mining, and with it, Dun Kithas will see its glory restored once more.

Please, take this. It's been in my family for generations, but now... now it's time for it to taste blood again. You've earned it.

41857.title: Miregill Distraction
41857.description:
Bah! Troggs to the east, Dragonmaw to the north, ghosts to the south, and now murlocs?! At this rate, I wouldn't be surprised if a Dark Portal opened right in my own backyard!

Regardless, those blasted murlocs gathering near Grimwater River are becoming a real problem. Their numbers are growing, and if we don't cull them soon, they'll be a danger to our fishermen.

Bring me twelve murloc scales as proof of your deed, <race>. Let's remind those fish-folk whose waters they're trespassing in!
41857.progress: Where do those murlocs even come from...
41857.completion: Ah! Now that's a job well done, <race>. I'll see to it that our fishermen are notified—the waters should be much safer now, thanks to your efforts.

41858.title: Gargill the Butcher
41858.description:
By now, you've no doubt noticed that sizeable cave on the south bank of Grimwater. Some time ago, the Mirefin murlocs took it over, and now we can't exploit its resources because of them.

We need to strike and drive them out of that cave once and for all. It's been proven that the best way to rid a place of murlocs is to cut off the head—kill their leader.

A murloc named Gargill commands this miserable lot, but our fishermen know him by another name: the Butcher. He's slain many of our own and will slay many more if he's not stopped.

Your task is simple, <race>—kill Gargill and 8 Miregill Murlocs and Muckdwellers. That should be enough to drive them out of the cave for good!
41858.progress: And to think that I used to love fish...
41858.completion: The news of the Butcher's demise brings a certain satisfaction, I'll admit. Hopefully, that'll be the last we see of those murlocs. Now, I can finally focus on what truly matters—the war with the Dragonmaw. We've got bigger fish to fry.

41859.title: After All This Time
41859.description:
<The small box is rusty and opens only under heavy force. The pungent odor of mold and wet earth escapes, showing the contents to be nothing more than a folded note and a scruffy pendant. With utmost caution, you unfold the delicate paper, revealing letters of an old typography:

“Wolram, I never got the chance to thank you for everything or even apologize for what I’ve done. It hasn’t been long since you’ve passed, and I try to move on, but the guilt is tearing me apart still. You always told me to look forward with conviction and purpose in my heart and I intend to follow your advice. What I’ve done in Grand Hamlet was my biggest regret and you’ve paid with your life for it. I will atone for my misdeeds by continuing your legacy, I will vow it on my father’s pendant. Please, safeguard it until I have fulfilled this vow, so that I may place it upon his grave free of doubt.

- Edrin”

Looking at the pendant, you ponder where that grave may be.>
41859.progress: <The grave has long been overgrown, yet the cross is still somewhat intact.>
41859.completion: <Carefully you dig a small hole into the ground. Wrapping the pendant around itself, you lay it softly into the fresh soil, before covering it again in veneration to the dead. For but a moment silence lays upon Elwynn, a warm breeze whispers through the trees and serenity sets in. Performing a last service of respect for Sir Vellas, his parents and Sir Notleigh, you stand in silent contemplation, before continuing on your path.>

41860.title: Emerald Summon
41860.description:
<name>, it is good to see you. Not long ago, a stranger was looking for your presence. I had told them I could relay a message, after which they told me the following:

“Meet us at the archdruid's barrow den. We will await your arrival.”

Mysterious, but there was no malice coming from them. I am sure you have nothing to fear.
41860.completion: Moonglade's tranquility is serene today, don't you think?

41861.title: The Dreamer's Challenge
41861.description:
We see our message has reached you, <name>. Word of your deeds has travelled far, even to the verdant stretches of the Emerald Dream. Your heroic service to Malorne has not gone unnoticed. His brethren, the Wild Gods, and his dear friend Ysera owe you much for saving him from the clutches of the Nightmare. Once he regains his form, we will gain another powerful ally against the dark entity within the Nightmare's miasma.

Our mother Ysera sent us to the sacred Moonglade in search of the one druid who opposed the Nightmare headfirst. To reward him for their actions in Hyjal and the Twilight Grove. That we will do. However, a test first. We know what you are capable of - your wit, strength and perseverance are unparalleled. Prove to us once more the extent of your abilities and we shall grant you more power to the blessing the Waywatcher bestowed upon you.

We will not hold back; be prepared to face the power of the Green Dragonflight!
41861.progress: Failure is no weakness, but simply a sign of growth waiting to happen.
41861.completion:
<Rethevus is breathing heavily. The fight has left him deeply exhausted.>

Incredible! What we heard about you was not an understatement, your mastery over Cenarius' teachings is as clear as a star-clad sky! Knowing a skilled individual like you to be on our side lets our heart rest easily. We made a promise to you and mother, a promise we shall keep. Here, receive the blessing of the Green Dragonflight. You are more than worthy of it.

For now, we bid you farewell. Mother awaits us in the Emerald Dream, where the war rages on still. The day when we will see eachother in the verdant expanses cannot come sooner.

41862.title: The Dragonmaw War
41862.description:
Welcome to Dun Kithas, friend. I'd gladly speak of our town's history and pride, but now isn't the time for stories.

As you've likely noticed, we're in a grim situation. The Dragonmaw clan has risen again, and we're knee-deep in a conflict we're steadily losing.

Your arrival, along with what few Alliance forces made it this far, gives me a sliver of hope. Perhaps there's still a chance we'll see the sun rise over these mountains again.

My most trusted commander, Mountaineer Steelwind, is holding position at East Ridge Outpost, north of Baggoth's Wall. He's leading the effort against the Dragonmaw and could use every capable hand we can spare. Head there at once and report in.
41862.completion:
Another Alliance adventurer, is it?

Good to know Ironforge hasn't abandoned us completely—though I'd have preferred reinforcements before things reached this sorry state.

Ah, don't mind the grumbling. I'm just an old dwarf with too many battles behind him and not enough warriors at his side.

We've got work to do and Dragonmaw to send back to the dirt. Let's not waste time.

41863.title: The Dragonmaw War
41863.description:
They're everywhere.

On the roads, in our old fortresses, in the caves, and scattered throughout the hills. Every caravan needs a dozen mountaineers just to reach its destination—and even then, the Dragonmaw strike more often than not.

This is a disgrace to Baggoth's memory... and a stain on my own honor.

We've endured enough. It's time the Dragonmaw learned that the dwarves of the Grim Reaches will not tolerate this humiliation any longer.

We strike back. We ambush them. We show them who truly rules these mountains.

Slay as many as you can, and bring me twenty of their sigils as proof. Let them know what it means to cross a Wildhammer.
41863.progress: I've sent a sizeable patrol to investigate what's left of Stolgaz Keep... but I haven't heard a word since.
41863.completion:
Ha! That will make them think twice before showing their ugly faces again.

This many Dragonmaw lying dead in the dirt should remind them to fear the Wildhammer Clan. With their numbers thinned, our caravans from Dun Kithas might finally get some breathing room.

Well done.

41864.title: The Dragonmaw War
41864.description:
There's one thing I can't abide — leaving behind the banner of a true dwarven hero.

When the Dragonmaw overran Baggoth Rampart, we were forced to retreat faster than I'd care to admit. In the chaos, our standard — the personal banner of Commander Baggoth himself — was left behind atop the central tower.

It's more than just a piece of cloth. That banner stood through a dozen battles and carries the pride of every dwarf who served beneath it. Letting it remain in orcish hands is an insult we can't stomach.

Climb the rampart, fight your way through the Dragonmaw scum, and retrieve that banner. Bring it back in one piece. For Baggoth. For the Reaches.
41864.progress: I'll not rest easy until that banner is back where it belongs.
41864.completion:
You've done us proud, lad.

To see this banner again… aye, it stirs the heart. The orcs defiled our walls, but they couldn't claim our spirit.

With this flying once more above Dun Kithas, our people will remember who we are — and what we're fighting for.

Well done.

41865.title: The Dragonmaw War
41865.description:
You've proven yourself more than capable, and now it's time we strike a real blow.

To the north lies Stolgaz Keep — or what's left of it. It was once a proud outpost, built stone by stone by the hands of dwarves who knew the meaning of endurance.

Now it's nothing but a shattered ruin, crawling with Dragonmaw filth. But don't let its current state fool you — the keep still holds strategic value. We take it back, and we've got a foothold to push further into the hills.

I need you to lead the charge. Get in there and cut them down. Slay twelve Dragonmaw Invaders, ten Renegades, and ten of those blasted Flamebinders.

And one more thing — their leader, a brute called Grathok Flamehand, commands the warband from the keep's inner sanctum. That orc's responsible for the destruction of the barracks and the burning of our supply stores.

End him. For the fallen. For Stolgaz.
41865.progress: Stolgaz Keep was named after my grandfather. I'll not see it left to rot under orc boots.
41865.completion:
Well done! That's a fine day's work — the screams of dying Dragonmaw are music to these old ears.

With their numbers thinned and the keep cleared, we can send a proper unit to reclaim and rebuild. You've done more for the Grim Reaches than most ever will.

Stolgaz Keep will fly the Wildhammer banner again, and it's thanks to you.

41866.title: Assault on Geth'kar
41866.description:
The Redbrand family holds sway across much of Khaz Modan—my father, Nazgrim, intends to make sure people are reminded of that.

He wants us to help out the folk here in Dun Kithas, lend a hand to the war effort and all that. Only trouble is... I'm not exactly the fighting type.

Still, it wouldn't hurt if word got around that I, Garlin Redbrand, made a real contribution to the cause.

North of here lies Geth'kar, a Dragonmaw fortress that's become a serious thorn in the Wildhammer's side. More importantly, it's their main supply depot. If you could sneak in and steal some of their supply crates—say, eight of them—it'd do real damage to their war effort.

And, well... let's just say it'd look good for the Redbrand name, too.
41866.progress: Be careful—Geth'kar is heavily fortified. I'm not joking!
41866.completion:
Well done, <class>! With these crates in our hands, the Dragonmaw will be scrambling to keep their forces fed and armed.

And no one can say Garlin Redbrand didn't do his part, eh? …Even if I did it through you.

41867.title: Blemishes on the Land
41867.description:
Ever since my team and I set foot in the Grim Reaches, I've had this nagging feeling in the pit of my stomach. There's something wrong with this place—something unnatural. The land itself feels... sick. The trees, the beasts, even the wind—it's all touched by a strange corruption.

Worse yet, I've seen it take shape. These oozes—shadowy, vile things—are crawling out of the hills like infection from a wound. Wherever they go, they spread that same rot to the land around them.

I need to understand what we're dealing with here. If you come across any of those oozes, would you mind… collecting some samples for me? Just, uh, try not to get any on yourself. I'll make it worth your while.
41867.progress: Be careful out there. The oozes might not look like much, but they're not the only twisted things lurking in the dark.
41867.completion:
Urgh, that smell could knock out an ogre!

<Dorthas winces and carefully takes the leaking samples from you>

Exactly as disgusting as I imagined... but unfortunately, also exactly what I needed.

<He peers closer, his expression shifting from curiosity to concern>

Hmm. I was afraid of this. The corruption's deeper and more complex than I thought. We're not just dealing with sick wildlife—something bigger is behind all this.

41868.title: Shadow Curse
41868.description:
We didn't just throw our tents down wherever the wind took us. There's a reason we're here.

Right behind us is an old cave—more like a tunnel, really. And where does it lead? Grim Batol. Or what's left of it. Don't panic, though—the main city is blocked off. The deeper halls collapsed ages ago. What we can reach is just some forgotten outpost, part of the outer ruins.

We tried poking around, but didn't get far. Wraiths drove us back—Wildhammer spirits, probably fallen during the Battle for Grim Batol. Only… something's off about them. They're not just restless. They're tainted, like those oozes you found.

I need more proof. If you're willing to head down there, put those spirits to rest and bring me back anything you find—samples, cursed residue, anything—I think we'll finally be able to piece together what's going on here.
41868.progress: Wish I could go with you, but... well, I learned the hard way I'm better with books than blades.
41868.completion:
<Dorthas squints at the samples, turning them over in his hands. His expression darkens.>

Just as I feared… this isn't some random corruption. This is the Shadow Curse—the same blight Modgud unleashed on Grim Batol during the war.

And it's still active. Even after all these years, the curse is seeping out, spreading past the ruins. Stone can't hold it back. Time hasn't weakened it. If no one acts… this whole region could fall. This is beyond anything we can handle alone. I'll send word to the mages in Dalaran. They need to know what's happening. As for us… all we can do now is keep watch—and pray.

41869.title: Death to Grimscale
41869.description:
Bah! May the Twisting Nether take the magistrate and their damn excuses!

All they care about are the bloody Dragonmaw orcs, while those Grimscale beasts run wild and tear through travelers like straw dolls.

They stood by while my only boy was torn apart out there. My son. Dead—because they sat on their hands.

I can't bring him back... but I sure as stone can stop this from happenin' to another dwarf's kin.

Go out into those hills. Hunt down eight of those Grimscale Raptors and their screechin' cousins. Cut 'em down, every last one. Then come back to me, and we'll see if there's still some justice left in this world.
41869.progress: My lad's blood cries out for justice. Don't come back until you've made those beasts pay.
41869.completion:
Ha! Now that's what I'm talkin' about! You did more with your blade than the whole damn magistrate's done in years of flappin' their gums.

You gave those monsters what they deserved, and maybe—just maybe—we can walk these roads again without fear.

Thank you, friend. My son would've been proud.

41870.title: Grimscale Revenge
41870.description:
So... you cut down the little ones. Good. But that was just the start. Just the bloody surface.

The real nest—where they get big, strong, and deadly—is up north of Lake Kithas. A blasted plateau up there, crawling with the worst of 'em. Grimscale Thrashers. Vicious, clever, fast as lightning. That's where they breed. That's where the heart of this filth festers.

The magistrate calls it a natural cycle. Bah! There's nothing natural about watching your boy scream as beasts tear him to pieces while you're too far to do a damn thing!

If you wipe enough of them out, maybe—just maybe—the mountain patrol will get their heads out of their arses and finish the job.

Slaughter them. Do it for me. Do it for my lad. Do it so no other dwarf has to bury their own flesh and blood.

I'd ride with you if I could, but these old bones can barely swing a tankard, let alone a blade.
41870.completion:
<Harfig listens closely as you recount the battle. His weathered face softens for the first time. A faint, tired smile creases the edges of his mouth.>

Aye… that's the news I've been needing to hear. You gave 'em hell, didn't you? I can feel it in my chest—like a weight's been lifted, if only a little.

I'll never hold my son again… never hear his laugh echo through the halls…

But thanks to you, some other parent might.

41871.title: Preparations for War
41871.description:
Aye, a new face in Dun Kithas!

Welcome to our mountainhome. It may not be as grand as Grim Batol, but don't let the modest stone fool you—we dwarves here are as sturdy and proud as the mountains themselves.

Still... things haven't been easy of late. The Dragonmaw orcs have returned in full force, and while our warriors are as strong as any to swing a hammer, we're sorely outnumbered.

Magistrate Hurdam Toughhand is leading our efforts. He's ordered any able-bodied adventurer—such as yourself—to report directly to him. You'll find him in the Magistrate's Hall, just up the path behind me. Big stone building, hard to miss. He's usually on the bottom floor, in the Council Hall.

Go on then, lad. Dun Kithas could use another strong arm.
41871.completion:
Ah, good—another strong back and keen blade.

I hope your travels were light and that you enjoy your stay in Dun Kithas, though there'll be little rest here, I fear. There's work to be done, and no time to waste.

41872.title: Provisions for War
41872.description:
Baggoth's Wall stands! But let me tell ye, it ain't standin' on full bellies…

This war with the Dragonmaw dogs has been hard on our folk. The countryside's crawling with threats, and our farmers—gods bless 'em—are holed up in Dun Kithas, their fields left fallow.

We've been gnawin' on roots, berries, and tough old legumes for months! And let me tell ye—this is no diet for a proper dwarf. I need a solid boar flank, roasted slow in beer, with thick-cut bread and butter to soak up the drippin's…

Ahem! But more than cravings, it's morale. My lads on this wall fight day and night, and they haven't seen meat in weeks. We can't leave our posts, but you… you look like you've got strong legs and a good aim.

Go into the hills and bring back fresh Stonehide Boar Flanks. The wall and Dun Kithas both will thank ye for it.
41872.progress: I would do anything for a proper feast.
41872.completion:
<Mountaineer Lightboots leans in and sniffs the meat with an almost reverent sigh.>

By the stones! That smell… it's glorious!

Now where's that blasted cookpot? We'll boil some, roast the rest… or maybe dry it to keep for later… Ah, the possibilities!

Ye've done more than fill a belly, <race>. You've helped lift the spirits of a whole outpost. And believe me, that's worth more than any blade.

41873.title: Brangar's Journal
41873.description:
<The journal is bound in worn, cracked leather. Most of its contents chronicle the mundane routines of a hardworking dwarven farmer—weather reports, planting cycles, notes about livestock. Yet, toward the final pages, the handwriting begins to shake, the lines become erratic… the words darker.>

She tells me to stay here, yes. She tells me to stay.

Magistrate... they want to take her from me.

I won't leave, no. I will keep her safe. Yes.

I hear voices. Oh, I hear them.

They tell me to stay.

I must.

I will.
41873.progress: What is it? You found it at Brangar's old farmstead?
41873.completion:
<Historian Sternhand reads the journal in silence, flipping the final pages with furrowed brows. He exhales slowly, then closes the book with a firm thump.>

Hmm. I suspected something went wrong out there... but not this.

Brangar was once a proud dwarf. A good farmer. It's a tragedy what happened—whatever did happen.

<He gives you a long look.>

For the sake of his legacy, I'll... omit these final entries from the official records. Some things are best left forgotten.

Thank you for bringing this to me, <race>. You've done a service to our history, even if it's a grim one.

41874.title: The Lost Archives
41874.description:
Stolgaz Keep… now there's a name that stirs the embers of old pride and fresh grief.

Once a proud bastion of the Wildhammer, the Keep held a critical position in the defense of the Grim Reaches. But that was before the Dragonmaw Orcs overran it. It has stood in enemy hands for years now—bastardized, defiled, but still standing.

What truly pains me isn't just the loss of the fortress… it's what was inside. The Keep housed some of our most precious historical records. Lineages, royal decrees, journals of heroes long gone—entire volumes chronicling the rise of our people.

Now, I doubt the Dragonmaw have the wit or care to destroy books. They likely don't even realize what they've taken. If you manage to reach the inner halls of Stolgaz, keep your eyes open. Any volume you retrieve could restore a piece of our history.

You do that, and I'll make sure you're well compensated.
41874.progress: Did you make it to Stolgaz? Any sign of the archives?
41874.completion:
<Sorgan's eyes widen as he takes the worn tomes into his hands, brushing centuries of dust from the covers.>

By the Makers… I never thought I'd see this again. This one—Baggoth's Testament! It's a first-hand account of the siege of Firewatch Ridge! Incredible!

You've done more than fetch books, <race>. You've helped restore the soul of our people. I'll be poring over these for days.

Who knows what secrets of the past we'll rediscover?

41875.title: Repairing Baggoth's Wall
41875.description:
Baggoth's Wall has stood through more Dragonmaw assaults than I care to count. But stone doesn't mend itself, and after years of siege and neglect… she's beginning to give.

Cracks run along the battlements, mortar has crumbled, and I've seen a goblin cannonball punch straight through one of the parapets. And to make things worse, stone shipments from the south are delayed—as always.

But the Reaches have always been built on bones of the past. Ruins of old dwarven strongholds and watchposts lie scattered across the region, their bricks still strong beneath moss and mud. With some work, they'll serve just fine to patch the wall.

Find any sturdy bricks or carved stones you can. Old ruins, abandoned outposts, even collapsed keeps—gather whatever can be repurposed. Every stone you bring helps keep Dragonmaw blades out of Dun Kithas.
41875.progress: There's rubble and ruin aplenty out there. We just need to be smart enough to use it.
41875.completion:
<Mountaineer Lightboots taps one of the bricks, nodding in approval.>

Solid stone… good heft to it. These will hold, once the masons get their hands on ‘em.

Well done, <race>. You've helped hold the line—for now. May the wall stand a little longer thanks to your effort.

41876.title: Ore Must Flow
41876.description:
Welcome to Slatebeard's Forge—where the sparks fly, the hammers sing, and the steel holds the line.

We've been outfitting mountaineers here for generations. Armor, axes, crossbow bolts—every piece forged with pride. But lately… pride won't keep the forge hot. The war effort demands more than we can handle, and we're nearly out of iron.

Normally I'd send my son down to Dun Kithas to fetch an update on the next ore shipment. But I've barely had time to breathe, and he's hammering like a madman as it is.

Would you do us a kindness? Head to Dun Kithas and ask Magistrate Toughhand when we can expect more ore from the Sal'Galaz mines. If it doesn't come soon, we'll be pounding steel with spoons…
41876.progress: You've come from Slatebeard's Forge, have you? I feared this moment would come.
41876.completion:
<Magistrate Toughhand strokes his beard and sighs.>

I'm afraid there's no easy answer. Sal'Galaz mines are overrun with troggs—filthy pests—and the miners have been driven out.

Without ore, the forge falls silent. And without the forge… well, let's just say our mountaineers might be going into battle with rusted blades.

We'll have to find a solution. Fast.

41877.title: Ore Must Flow
41877.description:
Even if we manage to reclaim the Sal'Galaz mines—which, mind you, I am working on—it'll take weeks for our miners to clear the tunnels, restore the scaffolds, and resume regular ore shipments.

And we don't have weeks. Every moment lost is another sword unsharpened and another shield left unrepaired.

It's time I called in an old favor.

There's a dwarf back in Ironforge—Lord Nazgrim Redbrand. A powerful name, I know. But he owes me, and more importantly, he commands the ear of the Miners' Guild.

Travel to Ironforge and speak with Nazgrim. Tell him I sent you, and explain our situation. If he helps us, the forge might burn bright again before the week is out.
41877.progress: What business brings you from Dun Kithas?
41877.completion:
<Nazgrim folds his arms and listens intently. After a moment, a smile breaks through his stern expression.>

Hurdam Toughhand… I haven't heard that name in some time. A stubborn mule of a dwarf—but a loyal one. I owe him more than just words.

And besides, the folk of Dun Kithas have held the line longer than any of us expected. If not for their grit, the Dragonmaw would be knocking on Ironforge's gates by now.

Yes. I'll send word to the guild. You'll have your ore.

41878.title: Ore Must Flow
41878.description:
The ore will come.

I'll have my men in the Ironforge Miners' Guild reroute a few shipments starting today. Might slow down some other projects, but Dun Kithas needs it more. Hurdam was right to act quickly.

Now go—return to him and tell him that Ironforge stands with Dun Kithas. And let him know this makes us even.
41878.progress: Did you speak to Nazgrim? Please tell me he agreed.
41878.completion:
<Magistrate Hurdam exhales deeply, shoulders relaxing for the first time in days.>

So he agreed… By the Light, that's a relief. This will buy us the time we need.

I'll have couriers ready to receive the first shipment. Slatebeard's Forge will run hot again, and our defenders will have the steel they need.

You've done more than you know, friend. Dun Kithas is in your debt.

41879.title: Crystal Clear Impression
41879.description:
My father is one of the finest smiths in all of Grim Reaches, and everyone knows it. I've been trying to earn his respect for years, but no matter what I do, it never seems to measure up to what Margella makes. She's just… better.

But I've been working on something special—something that might finally change that. A mace, a true masterwork of mine. It's not finished yet, though. It needs something rare, something powerful that will set it apart from every other weapon on the wall.

I've heard that deep below the Stormwrought Ruins on Balor, there are glowing red crystals—Stormwrought Crystals. They're said to carry incredible power, and if I could set one into the mace's head, it might finally prove that I'm a worthy smith too.

If you're headed to Balor, could you bring one back for me?
41879.progress: Have you found the crystal yet?
41879.completion:
The crystal!

<Grukson turns it over in his hands, clearly impressed.>

It's just how I imagined it—absolutely perfect. This will make the mace something truly special.

I'd better get to work, then. Maybe this time… my father will finally see what I'm capable of.

41880.title: The Dragonmaw War
41880.description:
The time has come for us to strike at the heart of the Dragonmaw presence in the Grim Reaches.

Zarm'geth Stronghold lies in the northern wilds — a fortress carved from stone and iron, bristling with traps, walls, and orcs of the deadliest kind. Elite warriors, battle-hardened champions, and no doubt their cruel leader command from there.

This will not be a fight for one man alone. You'll need comrades at your side if you hope to break their lines and claim victory.

Your target is clear: kill ten Dragonmaw Elite and ten Dragonmaw Champions. Slaying so many of their elite warriors will no doubt break their spirit.

Bring them down, and you strike a blow that will echo through the mountains.
41880.progress: Zarm'geth is no place for lone wolves. Rally your allies and show those orcs the fury of the Alliance!
41880.completion:
By the ancestors' beards, you've done what many thought impossible.

With so many of their officers dead, the Dragonmaw war machine in the Grim Reaches will sputter and die.

Celebrate this victory, but stay sharp — the war isn't over, not yet.

Well done, friend. The mountain remembers.

41881.title: Brangar's Folly
41881.description:
Now, we've got meat in our bellies… but meat alone doesn't hold a line. What we really need is bread—long-lasting, filling, proper dwarven food.

There might be a solution, but it's a risky one…

Far to the northeast lies Brangar's Farmstead. Well—what's left of it. Folks call it Brangar's Folly now. Brangar was once the richest farmer in all the Grim Reaches, owner of endless golden fields.

When the Dragonmaw came, he refused to leave. Said he'd die before giving up his land. And so he did.

Some say he went mad in those final days… others whisper he was hiding something darker. I don't put much stock in tales—but one thing's for sure: no one's claimed the grain in his granaries. And if any of it's still good, we'll put it to use before the rot or worse takes it.

Head out there and see what you can find. Ten crates of grain should be enough to get a proper stockpile going.
41881.progress:
Be careful out there…

Scouts say Brangar's Folly is home to darker things now than orcs.
41881.completion:
<Mountaineer Lightboots pries open one of the crates, sifting the grain between his fingers.>

Hmm… aye, I've seen fresher grain in my days… but this isn't bad. Mold's only hit a few sacks. With a little work, most of it's usable.

<He pauses, glancing around, voice dropping to a low whisper.>

Still… you saw what that place has become, didn't you?

Good job, <race>. It's better we have this grain than whatever was lurking there. But if I were you… I wouldn't speak too loudly of what you saw. Some truths are better left buried.

41882.title: The Dragonmaw War
41882.description:
After all the blood spilled and steel swung, there's but one thing left to do—bring word of our hard-won victories to the Magistrate in Dun Kithas.

I can think of no finer <race> to carry this honor than you, friend. It's by your hand and the strength of your kin that we struck the Dragonmaw down and protected the Grim Reaches—for now, at least.
41882.progress: Have you been any assistance to Steelwind?
41882.completion:
<Magistrate Hurdam Toughhand listens intently, clearly impressed>

By the forge and stone, you've done more than I dared hope for! The folk of Dun Kithas and the Grim Reaches owe you a great debt. Take this reward as a token of our thanks.
